events.title: First adult baptisms in Zurich launch the Anabaptist movement
events.description: Conrad Grebel, Felix Manz and George Blaurock baptised one another as believing adults in Zurich. Fiercely persecuted, their movement gave rise to the Mennonites, Amish and Hutterites.
events.html: Conrad Grebel, Felix Manz and George Blaurock baptised one another as believing adults in Zurich. Fiercely persecuted, their movement gave rise to the Mennonites, Amish and Hutterites.

events.title: Louis XVI is guillotined in Paris
events.description: Convicted of conspiracy against the nation, the former king was executed in the Place de la Révolution. His death set revolutionary France against the crowned heads of Europe.
events.html: Convicted of conspiracy against the nation, the former king was executed in the Place de la Révolution. His death set revolutionary France against the crowned heads of Europe.

events.title: Jefferson Davis bids farewell to the US Senate
events.description: Following Mississippi's secession, Davis and four other Southern senators gave farewell speeches and resigned. Within weeks he was chosen as President of the Confederate States.
events.html: Following Mississippi's secession, Davis and four other Southern senators gave farewell speeches and resigned. Within weeks he was chosen as President of the Confederate States.

events.title: New York passes an ordinance banning women from smoking in public
events.description: The Sullivan Ordinance barred managers of public places from allowing women to smoke. Mayor George McClellan vetoed it two weeks later, but it reflected anxieties about women's changing roles.
events.html: The Sullivan Ordinance barred managers of public places from allowing women to smoke. Mayor George McClellan vetoed it two weeks later, but it reflected anxieties about women's changing roles.

events.title: Vladimir Lenin dies at Gorki
events.description: The founder of the Soviet state died aged 53 after a series of strokes. His body was embalmed and displayed in Red Square, and Stalin outmanoeuvred Trotsky and others to succeed him.
events.html: The founder of the Soviet state died aged 53 after a series of strokes. His body was embalmed and displayed in Red Square, and Stalin outmanoeuvred Trotsky and others to succeed him.

events.title: USS Nautilus, the first nuclear-powered submarine, is launched
events.description: First Lady Mamie Eisenhower christened Nautilus at Groton, Connecticut. Able to stay submerged for weeks, it sailed under the North Pole in 1958 and transformed undersea warfare.
events.html: First Lady Mamie Eisenhower christened Nautilus at Groton, Connecticut. Able to stay submerged for weeks, it sailed under the North Pole in 1958 and transformed undersea warfare.

events.title: Concorde begins commercial supersonic service
events.description: British Airways flew Concorde from London to Bahrain and Air France from Paris to Rio de Janeiro via Dakar. Flying at twice the speed of sound, Concorde served passengers until 2003.
